evidenceBoundary: Renderer/component and desktop-main deterministic tests plus TypeScript builds. A local packaged artifact exists but predates the current source revision and was not launched or rebuilt in this audit. No provider, browser automation, or external account was used.
proven: Adjacent successful tool calls are grouped without hiding an individual failed operation; terminal runs reconcile orphaned in-progress tool, worker, and approval rows to a truthful cancelled/interrupted state.

The composer remains mounted below the task surface, supports Agent/Chat mode, accessible Enter/Shift+Enter/IME behavior, and lifecycle-derived working or waiting status rather than a stale raw running flag.

Current plan/state is rendered through WorkflowProgress and the canonical lifecycle; the inspector projects commands, changed files, subagents, approvals, ForgeVerify evidence, repairs, completion decision, and terminal failure detail from durable events/work items.
Approval state is an ordered, idempotent queue. Reload hydration adopts the server's authoritative pending list, and resolving one approval cannot erase another.
Executed command history is visible as a Commands panel with status, duration, and bounded output. This is honestly named command history, not an interactive terminal.
notProven: The current source revision running as a rebuilt/installed Windows package. The available local package was built on 2026-09-21, before this audit's 2026-09-23 source state.

A dedicated live browser session panel or interactive PTY terminal. Browser actions appear only as governed tool activity, and the desktop intentionally presents completed/running command history rather than a terminal emulator.

Human usability, accessibility with assistive technology, responsive layout, or visual correctness on an actual packaged Windows window. Static markup and deterministic state transitions are not user-study evidence.
requiredNextEvidence: Build an isolated fresh Windows package from the current commit, run its full/interruption/recovery smoke suite against a temporary smoke root, and perform a manual accessibility/responsive pass. Add a dedicated browser or terminal presentation only after defining the user-visible state, redaction, lifecycle, and approval contracts for those surfaces.
